title: Separate valid BLOCK policy verdict from REFUSAL / CLI errors in assess exit-code contract
description:
## Background & Evidence
`assess/README.md:148-154` and `operator.json` map:
- `0` = `PROCEED`
- `1` = `PROCEED_WITH_RISK` or `ESCALATE`
- `2` = `BLOCK`, `REFUSAL`, or CLI syntax error

Conflating `BLOCK` (a valid, deterministic policy evaluation outcome) with `REFUSAL` / CLI syntax errors inside exit `2` breaks agent branching: an automation loop checking `$?` cannot tell whether its own CLI invocation was malformed / missing an input artifact or whether the policy cleanly judged `BLOCK`. Similarly, `PROCEED_WITH_RISK` vs `ESCALATE` require different agent behaviors.

## Goal
Align `assess` with `spine-rules` v2's extended exit-code resolution so valid policy decisions are cleanly separated from `REFUSAL` and CLI usage errors:
- Ensure `REFUSAL` / CLI error has a dedicated non-overlapping code distinct from `BLOCK` (e.g. documented contract in `operator.json` & `capabilities --json`, with a staged deprecation note if exit `2` shifts).
- Ensure `capabilities --json` and `operator.json` publish the exact `exit_codes` dictionary with `retryable` metadata.
- Add regression tests verifying every decision band (`PROCEED`, `PROCEED_WITH_RISK`, `ESCALATE`, `BLOCK`), `REFUSAL`, and CLI parse error returns its distinct documented exit code.
acceptance_criteria: assess cleanly separates valid BLOCK policy verdicts from REFUSAL and CLI errors in code, operator.json, capabilities --json, README, and regression tests.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at 40b1708 (clean tree, includes 8218efc): cargo test --test exit_contract = 7 passed running the REAL binary (proceed 0, proceed_with_risk 0, escalate 1, block 3 as a decision with refusal:null, refusal 2 with decision_band absent, missing artifact = refusal not block, CLI syntax error 2); cargo test --test golden_rules = 9 passed incl operator_manifest_describes_assess_contract; 0 ignored. Diff scan: removed assertions are the old expectations (BLOCK=2, PROCEED_WITH_RISK=1) replaced by the new-contract tests; no #[ignore], no loosened asserts. Matches spine-rules docs/exit-codes.md band table. NOT verified: pack/receipts or any script that halts on assess exit 1/2 (my rg across spine repos found none; textual only, pane also did not check); 'retryable' is an extra manifest field outside operator.v1 (schema tolerates it); fmt/clippy and the full sweep not re-run by me; behavior change PROCEED_WITH_RISK 1->0 and BLOCK 2->3 will break external scripts keyed on the old codes.

title: Add compact decision summary render modes without changing assess.v0 JSON
description:
Context:
`assess` already emits one deterministic decision artifact, but in multi-tool operator workflows people still end up wrapping its JSON output just to scan the decision band, matched rule, observed tools, required tools, and refusal state across many runs. Add optional compact summary render surfaces derived from the existing decision/refusal artifact so operators can scan outcomes quickly while the canonical JSON contract stays unchanged.

Deliverables:
- add an optional compact summary render mode for decisions and refusals
- add an optional TSV summary render mode with stable columns for shell pipelines
- include at least: tool, version, outcome, decision, matched_rule, risk_code, required_tools, observed_tools, witness state when relevant, and refusal code when present
- ensure summary modes are pure renderings of the existing decision/refusal object and never perform additional policy evaluation
- update README, AGENTS, and output-focused tests to cover the new surfaces

Non-goals:
- changing rule matching semantics or policy loading
- changing the `assess.v0` JSON artifact
- teaching `assess` to interpret upstream raw metrics beyond existing exact-match policy signals

Plan alignment:
- stays inside the plan's output boundary
- preserves the 'one decision artifact' invariant for JSON mode
- improves operator ergonomics without broadening assess into a different kind of tool
acceptance_criteria:
1. `assess` can emit compact summary and TSV summary views for both decision artifacts and refusals without changing existing JSON output.
2. Summary values are rendered from the existing decision/refusal object only; no extra policy logic is introduced.
3. README, AGENTS, and output-focused tests document and verify the new surfaces.
4. The canonical JSON contract remains backward compatible.
close_reason: Implemented compact summary and TSV render modes with witness-status aware refusal handling, docs, and full test coverage.

title: Guide agents to verify when assess receives compiled constraints
description:
## Scope
Tighten the refusal path when assess receives a compiled constraints artifact instead of a verify report.

## Deliverables
- detect compiled constraints input early and keep the refusal outcome
- include a next_command that shows verify on the constraints first, then assess on the resulting report
- keep the wording aligned with assess's role as decision classification over upstream evidence artifacts

## Out of Scope
- accepting compiled constraints directly in assess
- changing decision policy or report schema
- generic input autodetection beyond this artifact confusion

## Acceptance Criteria
- compiled-constraints input returns a refusal with a non-null next_command
- the suggested command orders the flow as verify first, then assess
- regression coverage includes the compiled-constraints misuse case and keeps the valid verify-report path green
close_reason: Released in v0.1.2 after adding verify-first guidance for compiled constraints.

comments.text: BLOCKED on a spine-rules defect (not edited, per rules). golden_rules_suite! cannot pass for ANY canonical operator.v1 manifest. Repro (scratch consumer crate, spine-rules b2a8149): a manifest with schema_version operator.v1, tool_version, commands, exit codes 0/1/2, env_vars, formats, side_effects, pipeline passes r006_operator_json_is_valid_operator_v1 but FAILS r002_r007_exit_codes_trinity and r007_refusal_codes_match_source with: operator.json must be valid JSON: Error("missing field `version`") at src/helpers.rs:18. Cause: helpers.rs deserializes into the v0 types::OperatorManifest, whose `version: String` and `subcommands` are required, while operator.v1 (and the published schema) spell them tool_version / commands. Putting both spellings in one file also fails: OperatorContract aliases version->tool_version, so serde rejects the duplicate field. Only legacy spellings (version, subcommands) with schema_version operator.v1 would pass the suite, but that manifest violates operator.v1.schema.json (requires tool_version and commands), i.e. working around the contract. Fix belongs in spine-rules (helpers.rs trinity/refusal helpers should parse contract::OperatorContract, or OperatorManifest needs aliases tool_version/commands). No assess code changed for bd-wtu; nothing committed. Reported to operator.

title: Lock assess schema artifacts and shared policy/bundle types
description: Lock the assess schema artifacts and the shared policy/bundle type surface needed by policy loading, bundle parsing, evaluation, and rendering, without owning refusal handling or final rendering behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- `schemas/assess.v0.schema.json` and `schemas/policy.v0.schema.json` are locked to the v0 contract in `PLAN_ASSESS.md`.
- Shared Rust types for policy files, canonical artifact basis entries, matched-rule identity, policy hash context, and decision-band primitives compile without refusal-routing logic.
- Contract tests cover: default rule must be last, non-PROCEED rules require `risk_code`, every provided artifact remains representable in the epistemic basis, and schema-required fields stay stable.
- This lane does not own refusal envelopes, witness records, or final JSON/human rendering code.
notes: Primary files: `schemas/assess.v0.schema.json`, `schemas/policy.v0.schema.json`, `src/policy/schema.rs`, `src/bundle/artifact.rs`, and any tiny shared non-refusal enums/types. Avoid taking ownership of `src/refusal/**`, `src/witness/**`, or `src/output/**` formatting code.
close_reason: done

title: Harden policy validation (dead rules, empty matchers, undeclared tools) and dotted-version tool derivation
description:
## Evidence (Source Audit)
1. `src/policy/validate.rs:11-42`: silently accepts non-default rules with `when: None` (silently skipped as dead rules at `src/evaluate/mod.rs:52-54`), accepts empty `ToolMatcher` `{}` (which matches everything unconditionally at `src/evaluate/matcher.rs:207-211`), and does not validate that tools referenced in `when` appear in `requires` (silent typo trap where a rule can never match).
2. `src/bundle/derive.rs:13-17`: `derive_from_version` rejects dotted version prefixes like `verify.report.v1` or `decoding.spine.v0` because `.` fails `is_valid_tool_name`, so artifacts without an explicit `"tool"` field fail with `E_BAD_ARTIFACT`.

## Fix
1. Reject non-default rules with `when: None` or empty `when` map, reject completely empty `ToolMatcher` blocks, and reject/warn when `when` references a tool not in `requires`.
2. In `derive_from_version`, derive the leading tool segment before the first `.` when suffix ends with `.v<digits>` (preserving explicit `tool` precedence).
acceptance_criteria:
- `policy::validate` rejects dead non-default rules (`when: None` / empty `when`), empty `ToolMatcher` blocks, and rules referencing tools missing from `requires`.
- `derive::canonical_tool(None, "verify.report.v1")` resolves to `Some("verify")`.
- Unit tests cover all validation rejections and dotted-version derivations.

title: Add generalized assess CLI typo recovery and align --render/--json conventions
description:
## Background & Evidence
Ensure `assess` meets the family intent-inference bar (Axiom 7): edit-distance-1 flag and subcommand typos exit cleanly with a single-candidate `did you mean '--...'?` hint (never guessing on ties), and `--json` / `--render summary` / `--render summary-tsv` interaction is documented and regression-tested.
acceptance_criteria: Edit-distance-1 flag/subcommand typos emit deterministic did-you-mean hints with regression tests.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at 14e3485 (HEAD == origin/main, clean tree, includes 3d64b54): CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 cargo test --test typo_recovery --test cli_shell --test golden_rules --test no_color -- --test-threads=1 = 8 + 12 + 29 + 2 passed, 0 ignored. Built binary: 'assess --josn', '--rendr json', '--outt x' each exit 2 and print clap's tip plus the tool's own 'hint: did you mean --json/--render/--out'. Diff scan of 3d64b54: no removed assertions, no #[ignore]; README documents --json/--render conventions and the typo behavior (one-edit, unique candidate, scope-aware). NOT verified: top-level subcommand typos (assess capabilites) are NOT detected by design (a bare word is an artifact path; documented in README); clap's own tip and the tool's hint are two independent suggestion paths that agree in the cases I ran; doctor/witness/e2e suites not rerun for this change; lib 40 and clippy/ubs are pane evidence I did not re-run. Open design point for the other typo beads (rvl bd-1gj, shape bd-tqea, profile bd-375, lock bd-1mv, pack bd-i2l): port this behavior per tool; spine-rules is a dev-dependency only, so no shared runtime code.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
Commit 3d64b54 (pushed to origin main). Contract pin: spine-rules rev 5ec6622 (spine-rules src/schemas unchanged on origin/main 9d731fa since that rev, so no bump needed).

Change: src/cli/mod.rs format_cli_error no longer special-cases four misspellings of --json. did_you_mean() reads the clap error (UnknownArgument -> InvalidArg, InvalidSubcommand), resolves the command the user was inside from clap's usage line, builds candidates from that command's long flags (+ visible aliases, --help) or its subcommand names (+ help), and emits ONE `hint: did you mean `X`?` only when exactly one candidate is one edit away (optimal-string-alignment: insert/delete/substitute/adjacent swap, so --jsno->--json). Ties and far misses give no hint. The existing `next:` / `help:` lines are kept. Hints are stderr only, exit stays 2, stdout empty.

Tests (real binary, tests/typo_recovery.rs, 8 tests): flags --jsno/--josn/--jso/--polcy/--no-witnes/--rendr/--descibe each give exactly one hint naming the right flag; subcommands witness qurey->query, witness cuont->count, doctor triag->triage, doctor helth->health; scope: `doctor --polcy` gets NO hint (doctor has no --policy) while `witness last --josn` still gets --json (global); no hint for --completely-unrelated, --js, doctor --fix, witness everything; next/help lines kept; --json + --render summary is a usage error (2, empty stdout); an invalid --render value lists summary and summary-tsv; --render summary is one line, summary-tsv is header + one row. Unit tests in src/cli/mod.rs: swap/insert/delete distance, unique candidate, TIE gives None (--jon vs --json/--join), nothing close gives None. README Output Modes documents the --json/--render exclusivity and the typo rules.

Ran (one cargo command at a time, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3, all ok): cargo test --test typo_recovery (8), --test cli_shell (12), --lib (40), --test golden_rules (29), --test no_color (2); cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings (clean after fixing an index loop and test-module placement); ubs Critical 0.

NOT verified: top-level subcommand typos (assess capabilites) are not detected — a bare word is an artifact path by design, documented in README; clap's own `tip: a similar ...` line still appears alongside our hint (two suggestions, they agree in the cases tested but are independent code paths); doctor/witness/e2e suites not rerun for this change (only the files above); other tools do not yet share this implementation — the 'one consistent behavior across tools' beads (rvl bd-1gj, shape bd-tqea, profile bd-375, lock bd-1mv, pack bd-i2l) still need a decision on whether to copy this logic or extract it.
